dataset.description:
The goal of this interview is to identify the potential for implementing industrial symbiosis in the Liepaja region by evaluating the use of biomass ash from cogeneration for the production of blended cements in the construction industry. The research is led by qualified researchers with extensive experience in circular economy, material science, and regional development.
Experts and stakeholders—including energy producers, cement manufacturers, municipal representatives, and logistics companies—will be recruited, selected, and interviewed. The interviews will aim to assess stakeholder readiness, identify potential collaboration opportunities, and evaluate barriers and benefits of industrial symbiosis. Participants will be selected through targeted sampling using existing networks and professional contacts within the regional energy and construction sectors.
Each participant will receive a personalized electronic invitation explaining the research objectives and the significance of their participation. The invitation will highlight the confidential and voluntary nature of the study. Data collected from the interviews will be anonymized and analyzed both qualitatively and quantitatively to inform the development of an industrial symbiosis implementation plan and a digital stakeholder map.

dmp.description:
Development grant No RTU-PA-2024/1-0012 under the EU Recovery and Resilience Facility funded project No. 5.2.1.1.i.0/2/24/I/CFLA/003 “Implementation of consolidation and management changes at Riga Technical University, Liepaja University, Rezekne Academy of Technology, Latvian Maritime Academy and Liepaja Maritime College for the progress towards excellence in higher education, science, and innovation”.
The project aims to generate new scientific knowledge and technological insights by exploring industrial symbiosis opportunities in the concrete industry, specifically focusing on the use of biomass ash from cogeneration as a secondary raw material in blended cements. The novelty of this research lies in demonstrating the feasibility of using up to 20% biomass ash as a clinker substitute to create low-carbon concrete, integrating circular economy principles with sustainable construction.

Research activities include mapping industrial symbiosis potential in the Liepaja region, developing a digital mapping tool, conducting multi-criteria and life cycle assessments, and optimizing binder and concrete compositions using treated biomass ash. The study evaluates the environmental and economic impacts, identifies suitable circular business models, and assesses the applicability of developed materials in various construction scenarios, including roads, buildings, and infrastructure.

The expected outcome is a methodology for producing environmentally friendly blended cement concrete, a validated circular economy business model, and a pilot project demonstrating regional industrial symbiosis. The project will publish two scientific articles (including one Q1 publication in collaboration with a QS WUR TOP500 researcher), organize a seminar, involve two thesis-level students, and prepare an international Horizon Europe project proposal.
